topic.title: SQS vs SNS vs Kinesis vs EventBridge — choosing the messaging service
topic.concept: Four AWS messaging services, each for a different pattern: queue/pull, fan-out push, ordered replayable stream, and rule-routed event bus.
points: SQS: pull-based queue, at-least-once, visibility timeout; FIFO variant gives ordering + exactly-once at 300 msg/s (3000 batched).
SNS: push fan-out to many subscribers; pair SNS→SQS per consumer for durable fan-out.
Kinesis: ordered, replayable shards — 1MB/s or 1000 records/s ingest per shard, 2MB/s egress shared unless enhanced fan-out (2MB/s per consumer); retention up to 365 days.
EventBridge: event bus with content-based routing rules and schema registry — integration glue, not throughput.
Decision rule: need replay or ordering → Kinesis; work distribution → SQS; broadcast → SNS; cross-service routing → EventBridge.
topic.angle: 'Why Kinesis and not SQS here?' — the probe is whether you reason from replay/ordering/consumer-count requirements, not service familiarity. Know the shard math cold.
